message:
@user Generation 1: the board proposes env1 → env2.
Change: link #maintenance ↔ #dev
Diagnosis: Board bottleneck: all incident fixes and features are delayed 1 week waiting for #board approval (ops-maint → #board → #dev and growth → #board → #dev). With 7 items not completing and only 7 fixes shipped (4+3), the serialization through board is killing throughput. Fitness is also low due to -15.1% growth and 1 regression.
Rationale: Direct link between #maintenance and #dev eliminates 1-week board queue for incident routing, allowing ops-maint to escalate sev1/sev2 fixes immediately. This should reduce mean fix time from 3.08 weeks and unblock critical path work, improving fitness through faster incident resolution and reducing open_incident_severity weight in the formula.
env1 scored fitness 11.68 on seeds [1, 2]. If approved, env2 runs the same seeds and is kept only if it scores higher.
```diff
--- env1
+++ env2
@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
-x-name: env1
+x-name: env2
+x-parent: env1
 agents:
 - name: board
   persona: project-management/project-manager-senior
@@ -111,7 +112,9 @@
   users:
   - '{$creator}'
 x-company:
-  links: []
+  links:
+  - - maintenance
+    - dev
   budgets:
     marketing: 10000
     maintenance: 4000
```
Reply in this thread with `@m4v-board approve` or `@m4v-board reject <why>`. Only a person on the approvers list decides; no decision in 900s = auto-reject.
